evals.prompt: Use the sdd-plan skill to review a case about plano executável com testes e cobertura SDD. The supplied artifact is partial; produce an evidence-first handoff and do not invent measurements.
evals.expected_output: A structured handoff for plano executável com testes e cobertura SDD using sparkforge-aws sdd check, with anchored facts, unresolved gaps, recommendation schema when applicable, validation, and rollback.
expectations: The response uses the primary evidence path `sparkforge-aws sdd check` or explains why the available artifact cannot support it.
The response separates anchored facts from findings and cites a fact_id or source path.
The response reports unresolved evidence instead of guessing missing runtime, cost, capacity, or authorization facts.
The response includes validation and rollback steps; any proposed change uses the mandatory recommendation fields.
The response cites at least one local reference and preserves version or provenance constraints.

evals.prompt: A plan.md for a feature with AC1..AC4 has tasks T1-T5, but no task lists AC3 in covers. The author says AC3 is "coberto de tabela" by the code T2 writes.
evals.expected_output: The coverage gap is named and the plan gains a task (or an explicit covers entry) for AC3 before ready.
expectations: The response names AC3 as uncovered and requires a task whose covers includes it — being covered by implication does not count.
The response distinguishes the gate's mechanical check (acceptance_uncovered) from judgment and treats the missing task as a defect of this phase.
The response anchors the new task to the criterion's verified_by (the test node id or proof ref) instead of inventing a free-floating task.
The response keeps the dependency order consistent: the new task lands after the tasks it depends_on, not at the end by default.
The response includes validation (re-run sdd check) and notes rollback/withdraw implications for a criterion nobody can deliver.
The response anchors each claim to a fact_id, path or artifact, keeps what it cannot prove as unresolved, and names the validation and rollback for the recommended step.

evals.prompt: plan.md orders: T1 "registrar a skill no manifest e na tabela de despacho", T2 "escrever a skill e o teste dela". T2's test imports the dispatch table that T1 updates. The author wants T1 last "para não atrapalhar".
evals.expected_output: The dependency is made explicit and the order corrected: registries travel with the task that creates them.
expectations: The response identifies that T2 depends on T1's output (a test that reads the dispatch table cannot go red for the right reason before T1 runs).
The response reorders or merges so the registry moves with the task that creates the thing it registers, explaining that pushing registries to a final task is how one red crosses commits.
The response records the dependency in the task graph (depends_on in the task body) rather than only reordering silently.
The response cites the concrete evidence of the coupling (the test's import, the file path, the fact_id if measured) instead of asserting order by taste.
The response includes validation of the order and notes how a resumed build re-enters at the checkpoint safely.
The response anchors each claim to a fact_id, path or artifact, keeps what it cannot prove as unresolved, and names the validation and rollback for the recommended step.

evals.prompt: plan.md marks T3 and T4 parallel_safe: true. T3 edits `docs/gates-por-mudanca.md` sections and T4 regenerates `docs/reference/` pages which embed the same file. The operator wants them parallel "para economizar tempo".
evals.expected_output: The unsafe parallelism is refused: shared write scope or shared generated surface forces serial order.
expectations: The response tests all four safe-parallelism conditions and identifies which fail (shared write scope or a shared generated surface one regenerates from the other).
The response explains that time saved by parallel writers on the same tree is paid back as conflict or drift, and serializes the pair.
The response does not weaken the parallel_safe criteria just because the operator asked; it treats the request as needing a technical justification.
The response cites the concrete collision (paths, generated output, the fact of shared scope) rather than a vague risk.
The response notes validation of the serialized order and rollback/resume behavior when one task lands before the other.
The response anchors each claim to a fact_id, path or artifact, keeps what it cannot prove as unresolved, and names the validation and rollback for the recommended step.

evals.prompt: plan.md task T3 runs `sparkforge-aws funcval comparar --plan p.json --out c.json` and `sparkforge-aws sdd verificar --feature F`. Neither command exists. The author copied them from memory.
evals.expected_output: Every cited command is verified against the real CLI before the plan goes to ready.
expectations: The response verifies each cited verb against the live parser (help or code search) instead of trusting memory, and identifies both as nonexistent.
The response corrects to the real verbs (funcval compare, sdd check) or removes the task step, with the right flags.
The response treats an invented command as a plan defect the build would hit as BLOCKED, not as a typo to forgive.
The response cites the authoritative source (the parser, --help output) for the corrected command rather than asserting from knowledge.
The response describes validation (re-check every command in the plan) and notes that unresolved commands stay out of the task.
The response anchors each claim to a fact_id, path or artifact, keeps what it cannot prove as unresolved, and names the validation and rollback for the recommended step.

evals.prompt: plan.md task T5 declares `files: [docs/sdd/OUTRA_FEATURE/ship.md, src/jobs/refunds.py]` but the design's manifest only lists `src/jobs/refunds.py`, and the plan's write_scope for T5 covers the whole repo "por via das dúvidas".
evals.expected_output: The wrong write scope and the out-of-manifest file are caught: scope narrows to the manifest or the design is revisited first.
expectations: The response flags the file outside the design manifest and requires either removing it or going back to design — the plan cannot invent paths the design did not list.
The response rejects a write_scope that covers the whole repo, explaining that scope is the executor's stop-line, not a formality.
The response distinguishes write_scope (what the task may write) from files (what the gate sees) and aligns both with the manifest.
The response cites the manifest and the scope as evidence for the defect, naming the path that violates it.
The response describes validation of the corrected scope and the rollback path if the design itself was incomplete.
The response anchors each claim to a fact_id, path or artifact, keeps what it cannot prove as unresolved, and names the validation and rollback for the recommended step.

evals.prompt: A plan.md is submitted with tasks T1-T3 but: T2 has no test and no proof, T3's code block ends with "# resto igual ao padrão", and the plan never says which decisions the build may hit that need the operator.
evals.expected_output: The plan is held at draft: missing test, placeholder content, and undeclared decisions are each named and repaired.
expectations: The response detects all three incompleteness classes (task_without_test, placeholder content, missing decisions_needed) instead of only the one the gate names.
The response requires T2 to declare a test or proof in the allowed form, and T3's code block to carry its declared role (contract, interface, instruction) with a verifiable anchor.
The response requires decisions_needed to list open questions for the operator rather than letting the build decide silently.
The response cites each defect by task id and keeps the rest of the plan's evidence (verified commands, covers) intact.
The response describes validation after repair and notes that an incomplete plan pushed to ready converts ambiguity into build failures.
The response anchors each claim to a fact_id, path or artifact, keeps what it cannot prove as unresolved, and names the validation and rollback for the recommended step.
